questions.q: What are Snowflake's three architectural layers?
options: Database storage, compute (virtual warehouses), and cloud services
Frontend, backend, and database
Staging, warehouse, and reporting
Free tier, standard tier, and enterprise tier
questions.explain: Snowflake is built from three independently scaling layers: storage (where data lives), compute (virtual warehouses that run queries), and cloud services (coordination — auth, metadata, optimization, access control).

questions.q: Why can two virtual warehouses of different sizes query the same table at the same time without slowing each other down?
options: They are separate compute clusters reading from the same shared storage layer, so they don't compete for the same CPU or memory
Snowflake automatically makes a duplicate copy of the table for each warehouse
Only one warehouse can actually run a query at a time in Snowflake
Warehouses share compute resources with each other by default
questions.explain: Because compute is decoupled from storage, each virtual warehouse is its own independent cluster — they read the same underlying data without contending for resources.

questions.q: What does the compute layer consist of in Snowflake?
options: Virtual warehouses — clusters of compute resources that execute queries against the storage layer
The physical disks where table data is stored
The Snowsight web interface only
A single shared server that all queries run on
questions.explain: Virtual warehouses are the compute layer — they do the work of running queries, but don't own or store the data themselves.

questions.q: On a traditional on-prem SQL Server setup, why does scaling for more concurrent workloads mean buying a bigger box for everything?
options: Because storage and compute live on the same box, so you can't scale one without the other
Because SQL Server has no concept of a query at all
Because SQL Server automatically separates storage and compute already
Because on-prem servers cannot run more than one query per day
questions.explain: Storage and compute are coupled on the same hardware in a traditional on-prem setup, so scaling requires scaling both together even if you only need more of one.

questions.q: Why does suspending an idle virtual warehouse cost nothing?
options: Because storage and compute are billed separately, so a suspended (non-running) warehouse consumes no compute credits
Because Snowflake gives every account unlimited free compute
Because suspending a warehouse deletes the data it was using
Because warehouses are not billed at all, ever
questions.explain: Compute is billed by warehouse activity; when a warehouse is suspended it isn't running, so it isn't consuming credits — a direct consequence of storage and compute being separate layers.
